title: Rigveda 10.169: Blessing of the cows
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.169: Blessing of the cows: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.169 is a hymn of 4 verses addressed to blessing of the cows. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 147r-147v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
This manuscript inserts khila verses (supplementary hymns outside Aufrecht's text) at some hymn ends; they are noted in the section notes and not reproduced.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.169.1-2 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 27); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 147r
translation.original_text:
1ma̱yo̱bhūr vāto̍ a̱bhi vā̍tū̱srā ūrja̍svatī̱r oṣa̍dhī̱r ā ri̍śantām | pīva̍svatīr jī̱vadha̍nyāḥ pibantv ava̱sāya̍ pa̱dvate̍ rudra mṛḻa ||
2yāḥ sarū̍pā̱ virū̍pā̱ eka̍rūpā̱ yāsā̍m a̱gnir iṣṭyā̱ nāmā̍ni̱ veda̍ | yā aṅgi̍rasa̱s tapa̍se̱ha ca̱krus tābhya̍ḥ parjanya̱ mahi̱ śarma̍ yaccha ||
translation.text:
1MAY the wind blow upon our Cows with healing: may they eat herbage full of vigorous juices. May they drink waters rich in life and fatness: to food that moves on feet be gracious, Rudra.
2Like-coloured, various-hued, or single-coloured, whose names through sacrifice are known to Agni, Whom the Angirases produced by Fervour,vouchsafe to these, Parjanya, great protection.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 147r (OPenn image 146, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.168.3 ‹-katamac canāhaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 147v, begins in RV 10.169.3 ‹-somo viśvā rūpāṇi veda›. Verses 10.169.1-2 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.169.3-4 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 27); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 147v
translation.original_text:
3yā de̱veṣu̍ ta̱nva1̱̍m aira̍yanta̱ yāsā̱ṁ somo̱ viśvā̍ rū̱pāṇi̱ veda̍ | tā a̱smabhya̱m paya̍sā̱ pinva̍mānāḥ pra̱jāva̍tīr indra go̱ṣṭhe ri̍rīhi ||
4pra̱jāpa̍ti̱r mahya̍m e̱tā rarā̍ṇo̱ viśvai̍r de̱vaiḥ pi̱tṛbhi̍ḥ saṁvidā̱naḥ | śi̱vāḥ sa̱tīr upa̍ no go̱ṣṭham āka̱s tāsā̍ṁ va̱yam pra̱jayā̱ saṁ sa̍dema ||
translation.text:
3Those who have offered to the Gods their bodies, whose varied forms are all well known to Soma,– Those grant us in our cattle-pen, O Indra, with their full streams of milk and plenteous offspring.
4Prajâpati, bestowing these upon me, one-minded with all Gods and with the Fathers, Hath to our cow-pen brought auspicious cattle: so may we own the offspring they will bear us.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 147v (OPenn image 147, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.169.3 ‹-somo viśvā rūpāṇi veda›. 10.169.4 ends in line 3, followed by the heading khilaṃ and a khila (yāsām ūdhaś caturbilam) with a varga number in line 6; 10.170.1 begins at the end of line 6. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 148r, begins in RV 10.170.1 ‹-yajñapatāv avihrutam›. Verses 10.169.3-4 end on this page; 10.169.3 begins on fol. 147r.
